text: One autumn day, I called on my friend Sherlock Holmes and found him deep in conversation with a stout, elderly gentleman with fiery red hair. <break time="0.8s" /> The visitor, Mister Jabez Wilson, was a pawnbroker who had come to Holmes with a story that was very strange indeed. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes glanced at him and said that, apart from a few obvious facts, he could tell nothing about the man. <break time="0.8s" /> He has done hard work with his hands, he has been in China, and he has done much writing lately, he added. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Wilson was astonished at first, but when Holmes explained each clue, he laughed and said it was nothing clever after all. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he spread an old newspaper on his knee and pointed to a strange advertisement for the Red Headed League. <break time="0.8s" /> It said that the League had a job open for a red headed man, with a pay of four pounds a week for very little work. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Wilson explained that he kept a small pawnshop in Saxe Coburg Square, a quiet corner of the City of London. <break time="0.8s" /> His assistant, Vincent Spaulding, worked for only half the usual wages, and he was the one who had shown him the advertisement. <break time="0.8s" /> Spaulding had one fault, for he was always running down into the cellar to develop his photographs, like a rabbit into its hole.
